RoomType.rationale: BowlbugsWeak.cs:11 => RoomType.Monster. As with the Normal variant, the sim has no `room_type` field on `Encounter`; the pool-tuple placement (`weak_keys`, not `normal_keys`/`elite_keys`/`boss_keys`) is what the run layer reads to hand `RoomType.MONSTER` to `CombatState` at combat creation. Verified: "bowlbugs_weak" is in `_hive_rooms().weak_keys` only. Dynamic wiring into `CombatState.room_type` is seam/rooms_and_map's scope.

Tags.rationale: BowlbugsWeak.cs:13 declares EncounterTag.Workers. `_hive_rooms()` pins the identical single tag under "bowlbugs_weak". Same structural note as bowlbugs_normal: tags live at the room-picker layer (seam/rooms_and_map), not on the sim's `Encounter` object.

IsWeak.maps_to: rooms.py::_hive_rooms().weak_keys (pool-membership relocation, not a property on Encounter)
IsWeak.rationale: BowlbugsWeak.cs:15 `IsWeak => true`. The sim's `Encounter` dataclass has no `is_weak` field at all -- the concept is deliberately relocated one layer up: `RoomSet._generate_parity` (rooms.py) draws exactly `num_weak` rooms from `rooms.weak_keys` for the first `num_weak` slots of each act's `normal_keys` list (mirroring `ActModel.GenerateRooms`'s weak-count front-loading), and "bowlbugs_weak"/"exoskeletons_weak" are the only two Hive keys in that tuple, with their Normal counterparts absent from it. This reproduces IsWeak's actual behavioral role ("one of the weak encounters we start acts with") without a matching boolean property on the encounter object -- a structural, not behavioral, divergence.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no per-encounter counterpart; full_env.py::_monster_classes() (global Monster-subclass walk)
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: BowlbugsWeak.cs:17-23 declares {BowlbugEgg, BowlbugNectar, BowlbugRock} -- exactly GenerateMonsters' draw space. Same finding as bowlbugs_normal: the C# property's only two real consumers (`UnlockConsoleCmd.cs:68,147` dev-console unlock listing; `NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164` bestiary completion ratio) are debug/UI surfaces with no sim equivalent, and the sim's actual vocabulary need (`full_env.py`'s `MONSTER_IDS`) is satisfied by a global class-hierarchy walk that finds these three classes regardless of any per-encounter declaration. Cost: none observed.

HasScene.maps_to: no counterpart -- sim is headless, no Godot scene graph
HasScene.rationale: BowlbugsWeak.cs:25 => true. Same rationale as bowlbugs_normal's HasScene: purely a rendering-asset gate (`EncounterModel.ScenePath`/`CreateScene()`), no headless equivalent, no gameplay consequence.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: BowlbugsWeak.cs:27-34: the array literal is `{(Rock.ToMutable(), "odd"), (base.Rng.NextItem(Bugs).ToMutable(), "even")}` where `Bugs` is declared in the fixed order [Egg, Nectar] (BowlbugsWeak.cs:17-21). C# evaluates array-initializer elements left to right, so Rock's tuple element (no draw) is constructed before the second element's `NextItem(Bugs)` draw runs -- exactly 1 draw total, over a 2-item candidate set, roster order [Rock, worker]. `bowlbugs.py`'s `BowlbugsWeakEncounter.create_monsters` reproduces this: `bugs = [BowlbugEgg, BowlbugNectar]` (same order), `worker_cls = selection_rng.next_item(bugs)` (parity) drawn once, then `return [BowlbugRock(hooks, rng), worker_cls(hooks, rng)]` -- Rock first, worker second, 1 draw, same 2-item ordered candidate set. Slot strings "odd"/"even" are, like the Normal variant, cosmetic: `BowlbugsWeak` does not override `Slots` (stays empty), so `SortEnemiesBySlotName` is a no-op and no monster in this family reads `Creature.SlotName` in its own move logic (verified by the same cross-file grep as bowlbugs_normal). The sim's non-assignment of `slot_name` therefore costs nothing observable; roster order is what matters and it matches.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: Same as bowlbugs_normal: `EncounterModel.cs:39` default (`=> false`), not overridden by the sealed `BowlbugsWeak`; the sim's `Encounter` is never registered as a hook listener in `combat.py`.

guards.what: Gold ladder (MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward) and ShouldGiveRewards -- both inherited, not overridden by BowlbugsWeak
guards.rationale: Same ladder as bowlbugs_normal (RoomType.Monster => 10-20 gold, `rewards.py:170-173`), and `ShouldGiveRewards` default `true` matched by `Encounter.should_give_rewards`'s dataclass default, unmodified by `BOWLBUGS_WEAK = BowlbugsWeakEncounter(id="bowlbugs_weak")`.
